reasoning: The precondition is heavy: the attacker must be able to publish on the release repo. Given that, the claimed damage holds. (1) Source: every integrity input comes from the attacker's own release. The size comes from the asset metadata (UpdateChecker.swift:193). The SHA comes from a sibling checksums-*.txt asset in that release, fetched with try? (:179-186), and the check is skipped when it is nil (:259). (2) Dangerous operation: the DMG is moved into ~/Downloads (:265) and revealed in Finder (:275), and the user is told to drag the app into /Applications. (3) No effective mitigation: nothing in UpdateChecker checks the signature or team ID. CodeSignatureInfo.currentTeamID (Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Util/CodeSignatureInfo.swift:42) is never called from the update path. The download is a plain session.download (HTTPClient.swift:71) in an app that is not sandboxed (Resources/entitlements.plist:14-15, app-sandbox false). Resources/Info.plist has no LSFileQuarantineEnabled, and there is no xattr code. So the file gets no com.apple.quarantine flag, and the Gatekeeper check the comment at :267-274 relies on never runs for an unsigned app. The impact is real and specific: CLAUDE.md keeps the Developer ID key off the repo on purpose, so compromising GitHub alone should not be enough to ship code that runs. This path makes it enough. The result is arbitrary code running as the user, with access to the Claude and Codex credentials the app handles.
